datasets.title: French Guiana - Spatial Distribution of Population (2015-2030)
datasets.description: Estimates, total number of people per grid-cell. The dataset is available to download in Geotiff format at a resolution of 3 arc (approximately 100m at the equator). The projection is Geographic Coordinate System, WGS84. The units are number of people per pixel. The mapping approach is Random Forest-based dasymetric redistribution. More information can be found in the Release Statement Please note that these data represent 2025 Alpha release versions, constructed in September 2025. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/worldpop-population-counts-2015-2030-guf]
datasets.details: Disclaimer:The dataset currently represents an alpha version (R2025A) product and may change over the coming year as improvements are made. Data for earlier dates is available directly from WorldPop Bondarenko M., Priyatikanto R., Tejedor-Garavito N., Zhang W., McKeen T., Cunningham A., Woods T., Hilton J., Cihan D., Nosatiuk B., Brinkhoff T., Tatem A., Sorichetta A.. 2025 Constrained estimates of 2015-2030 total number of people per grid square at a resolution of 3 arc (approximately 100m at the equator) R2025A version v1. Global Demographic Data Project - Funded by The Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation (INV-045237). WorldPop - School of Geography and Environmental Science, University of Southampton. DOI:10.5258/SOTON/WP00839

lineage.description: Gridded population estimates derived from multiple source datasets using Random Forest-based dasymetric redistribution methodology. Population counts are redistributed to 100m and 1km grid cells across French Guiana for the period 2015-2030, providing spatially-explicit exposure data for disaster risk assessment.

sources.name: WorldPop
sources.description: Random Forest-based dasymetric redistribution model for gridded population estimation using multiple source data integrated into spatially-explicit population counts
